runs.title: WoW: Forever — UK launch time
runs.prompt: The next World of Warcraft expansion, 'World of Warcraft: Forever', launches globally on 4 November 2026. Find out the exact launch time in UK time (GMT), and note whether there is any pre-load/pre-purchase detail. Blizzard's own news page is a good first stop.
runs.answer: World of Warcraft: Forever launches as a single global go-live on Wednesday 4 November 2026 at 11:00 p.m. UK time (23:00 GMT/UTC — the UK is back on GMT by then, so no offset applies), which Blizzard lists as 3:00 p.m. PST. Pre-loading is available ahead of launch through the Battle.net launcher, and the client needs roughly 128 GB of free SSD space. There is no box price: the game is included with an active WoW subscription or Game Time, while optional pre-purchase packs are the Skyborne Heroic Pack ($29.99/€29.99), Skyborne Epic Pack ($59.99/€59.99, adds guaranteed beta access and 30 days of Game Time) and Warcraft Forever Collection ($79.99/€79.99); Heroic and above included Early Name Reservation for up to 3 characters from 27 October to 3 November 2026. Caveat worth noting: one Blizzard article reportedly gave 3:00 p.m. PDT, but every other official page and the site countdown match 3:00 p.m. PST / 23:00 UTC.

runs.title: Spain train crash: the Australians' status
runs.prompt: A high-speed train collision occurred near Toledo, Spain in late October 2026, and Australian authorities have now confirmed that two Australians died. Find out, respectfully and factually: (1) what precisely has been confirmed about the two Australians, and (2) where to find official or authoritative information (for example the Australian government's smartraveller consular advice or ABC News). Give facts, not speculation.
runs.answer: Spain's identification body (an Integrated Data Centre of police and forensic experts, announced by the High Court of Justice of Castilla-La Mancha) confirmed late on Monday 2 November 2026 that two Australians are among the 69 people killed when a Renfe train hit the rear of a stationary Iryo train outside Urda, Toledo province, on Wednesday 28 October; the other victims are 54 Spanish nationals and 15 foreigners (4 US, 2 Japanese, and one each from Argentina, Canada, France, Mexico, Portugal, Tunisia and Czechia). No names, ages or hometowns have been released: Spanish data protection law applies, and authorities say all victims' families and relevant consular officials have been notified (40 men and 29 women died, and identification work is complete). DFAT said on Friday 30 October that it was providing consular assistance to the family of two Australians and "working with local authorities to confirm the welfare of the Australians", declining further comment due to privacy obligations, with a spokesperson offering "heartfelt condolences". For official information use DFAT's Smartraveller site (smartraveller.gov.au — Spain destination page and its Consular Emergency Centre), DFA
